purpose: The six-item FAQ accordion, the last body section on the home page.

headingLines.note:
Exactly 2 lines separated by a
. Measured: "Not AI-gen answers." (3) and "Real ones here." (3).

question.note: Measured 6-8 words across all six items.

answer.note:
Measured 11-17 words across all six items; each is a single

.

icon.note: A literal plus character, not a glyph. public/motion/m13.js toggles the item's `active` class, which is what changes it.

items.note: Exactly 6 items. All ship collapsed (display:none, height:0px inline), so none is open by default.

evidence.structure: Structure, layout and motion measured against the live original. A pixel audit verified 1382/1382 elements at a 1440px viewport and 962/962 at 390px with zero deltas. Copy is the original's own.

constraints.verification: src/pages/Home.jsx:17 renders <Faq /> last inside <Layout>. Checked against all 5 real templates: it appears only in `home`, as the last body node before chrome.footer.

motion.detail: The h2 carries data-flash and runs the m22 + m23 split-and-reveal sequence. public/motion/m13.js drives the accordion: it binds click on .faq__item-title, toggles `active` on the item and animates .faq__content height.
motion.reducedMotionFallback: Render the heading unsplit at text.primary and open or close each item instantly, with no height animation. Keep every item closed on load, as the source does.
motion.reducedMotionFallbackKind: design-rule (the source ships NO prefers-reduced-motion handling for this section, so the fallback is prescribed by this repository, not mirrored)

responsive.base: eyebrow left, heading and accordion right; question at body.large 1.25rem, answer at body.default 1rem
responsive.max-991px: heading.display drops 7.5rem -> 5.5rem; both body steps unchanged
responsive.max-767px: heading.display 2.25rem, label.tag 1rem, body.large 1rem and body.default 0.875rem - question and answer nearly converge

measuredFrom.quote: What can AI FOURMULA create for my brand?
Does this replace my creative team?

contentMaxWordsTotalNote: Set BETWEEN the measured real total and the maximum the per-field budgets allow, so the cap can actually reject an over-long instance instead of being unreachable. extraction/verify_all.py check [p] fails if any declared contentMaxWordsTotal becomes vacuous (>= the per-field maximum). Previously 170, which was unreachable.
